raw.product_description: Narma is an "Enterprise Agentic Brain" designed for AI-first companies. It features a three-layered architecture. Layer 1 (Observe): uses lightweight desktop sensors to capture work patterns, application usage, activity sequences, and time allocation. Layer 2 (Intelligence Layer): a "Brain" that detects employee intent, business value of tasks, and "drift" in work processes. Layer 3 (Execution Layer): an "Agent Factory" that automatically generates, deploys, and monitors AI agents for high-ROI opportunities, with built-in approval gates. Narma leverages existing foundation models and focuses on building a "Work Graph" to identify resource drains and opportunities for AI intervention to assist mid-flow.

raw.thesis: Narma proposes an "Enterprise Agentic Brain" for AI-first companies to streamline AI automation. The core innovation lies in its three-layered architecture: Observe, Intelligence, and Execution. It aims to solve the problem of enterprises struggling with a lack of telemetry for AI savings, unreliable ROI measurements, and constant process drift by providing a single system that watches work, decides AI interventions, and continuously builds AI agents. This venture is for AI-first companies seeking to optimize their AI automation efforts. The founder seems to envision a growth-oriented startup given the emphasis on "at scale" and continuous AI lift. The current stage is at the idea phase as no artifacts or signals of development were mentioned in the intake. Narma positions itself as a complementary and optimizing layer on top of existing foundation models, rather than a replacement, by focusing on improving the utilization and impact of AI within an enterprise's existing infrastructure. It aims to reveal inefficiencies and deploy targeted AI solutions, thereby enhancing the value derived from current AI investments.
raw.one_liner: Narma is an "Enterprise Agentic Brain" designed for AI-first companies to see, prove, and deploy AI automation at scale.
